verses.1: And from there, he goes to the borders of Judea. He also crosses the Jordan River. Once again, people gather around him, and once more, he teaches them.
verses.2: And they asked him whether it was appropriate for a man to abandon his wife, trying to test him.
verses.3: And the one who answered said to them, “What did Moses command you?”
verses.4: And they said, “Moses was allowed to write and burn that book of prohibitions.”
verses.5: But Jesus said to them, “To your hard hearts I have written this commandment.”
verses.6: From the beginning of construction, he created them and made them alive.
verses.7: For this reason, a person will abandon his father and mother, and become attached to his wife.
verses.8: And the two will become one body. So, there will no longer be two bodies, but only one body.
verses.9: So, the God chose a person who would not be divided.
verses.10: And once again, the disciples asked him about this in the house as well.
verses.11: And he said to them: “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman, he is guilty of adultery against her.”
verses.12: And if she divorces her husband, then she can marry another man.
verses.13: And they brought their children to him, so that he might baptize them. The disciples agreed to do this.
verses.14: When Jesus saw this, he became angry and said to them, “Take the children away from here. Do not prevent them from coming to me. For it is through such people that the kingdom of God will be established.”
verses.15: I say to you, those who do not accept the kingdom of God as a child, shall not enter it.
verses.16: And he forced them to bend their hands over those objects.
verses.17: And as he was carrying him along on his journey, he comforted him and consoled him. “Good teacher, what should I do so that I may receive eternal life as a inheritance?”
verses.18: But Jesus said to him, “What do you call me good? No one can be called good except God.”
verses.19: You know the commands: Do not kill, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not lie, do not bear false witness. Also, do not harm your father and mother.
verses.20: And he said to him, “Teacher, I have kept all these things since my youth.”
verses.21: And Jesus, when he saw him, loved him and said to him, “Have courage! Sell what you have and give it to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven, and follow me.”
verses.22: But the man who was offended by those words left in a state of sorrow, for he had many possessions.
verses.23: And looking around, Jesus said to his disciples, “How difficult it is for those who possess money to enter the kingdom of God.”
verses.24: But the disciples listened to his words. Then Jesus answered them again, saying, “Children, how difficult it is to enter the kingdom of God!”
verses.25: It is better to die in poverty, rather than become rich and enter God’s kingdom.
verses.26: But they were greatly perplexed, saying to themselves: “Who can possibly survive?”
verses.27: When Jesus looked at them, he said, “It’s impossible for people to do this, but not for God. For everything is possible for God.”
verses.28: Peter began to speak to him: “Look, we have abandoned everything and followed you.”
verses.29: Jesus said, “I tell you, none of those who have left their homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, fathers, children, or fields because of me and because of the gospel can go away without being saved.”
verses.30: If he does not receive one hundred times more than what he has now, along with his brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and lands, then in the coming years, he will have to live a life of suffering.
verses.31: Many will be first in the end, and those who are last will also be first in the end.
verses.32: While they were on their way back to Jerusalem, Jesus led them along the road. As they walked, they were terrified. But when he took them aside again, he began to tell them what would happen to them in the future.
verses.33: For we are now going back to Jerusalem. The son of man will be handed over to the priests and scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the nations.
verses.34: They will also pierce him, wound him, and kill him. After three days, he will rise again.
verses.35: And Iacob and John’s sons, the sons of Zebedaeus, pretended to be with him, saying to him, “Teacher, we want you to tell us what you will do when we ask you a question.”
verses.36: And he said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
verses.37: But they said to him, “Let us sit one on your right and one on your left, in your glory.”
verses.38: But Jesus said to them, “Do you not know what you are asking for? Can you really drink from the cup I drink from, or be baptized with the baptism I baptize with?”
verses.39: But they said to him, “We cannot do this.” But Jesus said to them, “Drink from the cup that I drink, and bathe in the bath that I bathe.”
verses.40: But the seat that you sit on, whether on my right or on Eunymos’s side, I cannot give it to you. It must be given to those who are worthy of it.
verses.41: And when they heard this, the ten began to argue among themselves about Jacob and John.
verses.42: And when Jesus called them together, he said to them, “Do you know that those who try to rule over other nations do so in order to oppress them? And those who are powerful over others do so in order to exploit them.”
verses.43: It’s not like that among you. But anyone who wants to become important among you will be your deputy.
verses.44: And anyone who wants to be first among you will be a slave in every way.
verses.45: For indeed, the son of man did not come to serve, but to serve and give his own soul as a sacrifice in place of many others.
verses.46: And they went to Jerusalem. And as he was leading them away from Jerusalem, along with his disciples and the crowd, the blind man who was a disciple of Timothy Bar-Timaios sat down by the way.
verses.47: And when he heard that Jesus of Nazareth was there, he began to shout and say, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
verses.48: And many tried to make him remain silent. But he refused to do so. Son of David, please have mercy on me.
verses.49: And Jesus said, “Speak to him.” So they spoke to the blind man, saying, “Hearing me, please.”
verses.50: And when he threw off his clothes, he rushed towards Jesus.
verses.51: And when Jesus asked him, “What do you want me to do?” the blind man said to him, “Rabbi, let me see again.”
verses.52: And Jesus said to him, “Go, your faith has saved you.” Immediately, he looked up, and followed him on the road.
